classification.difficultyReason: No cue is given. The student must see that the diagonals bisect each other, or use ∠ABE-∠ABD, and then combine two or three trig steps. There is no scaffolding, and the angle needs a hidden construction or difference of angles.

content.prompt: In rectangle $ABCD$, $BE$ is perpendicular to $AC$. Find the size of $\angle EBD$ to 1 d.p.

answer.worked:
In $\triangle ABC$, $\tan\angle BAC=\frac{6}{8}$, so $\angle BAC\approx36.87^\circ$. In $\triangle ABE$, $\angle AEB=90^\circ$, so $\angle ABE$ is complementary to $\angle BAC$. In $\triangle ABD$, $\tan\angle ABD=\frac{6}{8}$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABE&=90^\circ-36.87^\circ\\\angle ABE&=53.13^\circ\\\angle ABD&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac68\right)\\\angle ABD&\approx36.87^\circ\\\angle EBD&=\angle ABE-\angle ABD\\\angle EBD&=53.13^\circ-36.87^\circ\\\angle EBD&\approx16.3^\circ\end{align*}$$
